problem: It says a faster link 'does not stop packets from overtaking each other in the queue'. A FIFO queue never reorders packets, so no overtaking happens; the real cause of jitter is that the queue length (and so the waiting time) changes from packet to packet, and a faster link only shortens each wait. A student will come away with a false picture of jitter as packet reordering.
fix: Jitter comes from queueing delay varying: a voice packet may find the queue empty one moment and behind a large data packet the next. A faster link shortens each wait but does not stop the queue depth from varying, so delay still varies unless scheduling gives each flow its own queue and a guaranteed share.

problem: The TSpec is defined with r and p in bits per second, and the trap states this as the rule. The standard TSpec (RFC 2210) expresses the token bucket rate, token bucket depth, peak rate, minimum policed unit and maximum packet size all in bytes (rates in bytes per second). The chapter is self-consistent, but the trap turns a local convention into a claim about the standard.
fix: Say: 'This book writes the rates in bits per second; the standard TSpec defines r, b, p, m and M all in bytes (r and p in bytes per second). Convert before comparing with link rates.' Change the trap to warn about mixing bits and bytes when converting, not to assert that TSpec rates are bits per second.

where: Figure 'What a reserved flow passes through'
problem: The chain puts admission control in the per-packet path between the classifier and the token-bucket policer. Admission control runs once, at reservation setup, not on every packet; only classification, policing and queueing are per packet. The caption hints at this but the boxes do not.
fix: Show admission control as a once-only step that decides 'admit or reject' for the flow before any packet is served, and let the per-packet path run packet → classifier → token-bucket policer → per-flow queue (WFQ) → output. Note that the last box is 'guaranteed or controlled-load service', since both classes use this path.
